items.fullText: 국제 로버트 패틴슨, 차기 '제임스 본드' 확정…'007' 시리즈 새 얼굴로 발행일 : 2026-11-17 09:06 전자신문을 선호 매체로 추가 공유하기 페이스북 X(트위터) X(트위터) --> 메일 URL 복사 글자크기 설정 가 작게 가 보통 가 크게 로버트 패틴슨. 사진=Jaap Buitendijk / 버라이어티 캡처 할리우드 배우 로버트 패틴슨이 영화 '007' 시리즈의 새로운 제임스 본드로 낙점됐다. 다니엘 크레이그의 뒤를 이을 차기 본드 역을 두고 수개월간 이어졌던 할리우드의 캐스팅 경쟁도 막을 내렸다. 16일(현지시간) 미국 연예매체 버라이어티(Variety)에 따르면 아마존 MGM 스튜디오는 패틴슨을 차기 '007' 시리즈의 주인공 제임스 본드 역으로 공식 확정했다. 패틴슨은 성명을 통해 “제임스 본드는 영화 역사상 가장 전설적인 캐릭터 중 하나”라며 “007 역할을 맡게 된 것은 평생의 영광”이라고 소감을 밝혔다. 이어 “드니 빌뇌브 감독과 아마존 MGM 스튜디오 관계자들이 나를 믿어준 데 깊이 감사한다”며 “꿈이 현실이 됐다는 말로도 부족할 만큼 기쁘다. 훌륭한 팀과 함께할 앞으로의 작업이 기대된다”고 말했다. 새로운 007 영화의 연출은 '듄' 시리즈로 유명한 드니 빌뇌브 감독이 맡는다. 빌뇌브 감독은 오는 12월 개봉 예정인 '듄: 파트 3'에서도 패틴슨과 호흡을 맞췄다. 빌뇌브 감독은 “이번 여정에 함께한 뛰어난 배우들에게 먼저 감사의 뜻을 전하고 싶다”며 “훌륭한 배우들이 많았지만 007은 단 한 명뿐”이라고 말했다. 그러면서 “로버트 패틴슨을 새로운 제임스 본드로 맞이하게 돼 매우 기쁘다”며 “그는 007의 시대를 초월한 정신을 지니면서도 완전히 새로운 매력을 선보일 배우”라고 평가했다. 이번 작품은 '스파이더맨' 시리즈와 여러 007 영화 제작에 참여한 에이미 파스칼, '해리포터' 시리즈의 데이비드 헤이먼이 공동 제작한다. 타냐 라푸앵트가 총괄 제작을 맡고, 영국 드라마 '피키 블라인더스'로 알려진 스티븐 나이트가 각본을 집필한다. 패틴슨은 2006년 개봉한 '007 카지노 로얄'부터 2021년 '007 노 타임 투 다이'까지 총 5편에서 제임스 본드를 연기한 다니엘 크레이그의 뒤를 잇게 됐다. 특히 이번 작품은 오랜 기간 시리즈를 이끌어 온 제작자 마이클 G. 윌슨과 바버라 브로콜리가 아마존 MGM에 프랜차이즈의 창작 통제권을 넘긴 이후 제작되는 새로운 007 영화라는 점에서도 주목받고 있다. 차기 제임스 본드의 주인공을 둘러싸고는 그동안 여러 배우의 이름이 거론됐다. 초기에는 '유포리아'로 유명한 제이콥 엘로디가 유력 후보로 떠올랐으나, 이후 실제 스크린 테스트에도 참여하지 않았다는 보도가 나왔다. 영국 배우 잭 로던 역시 후보로 거론됐다. 지난 9월에는 로던과 드라마 '슬로 호시스'에 함께 출연한 게리 올드먼이 이미 차기 본드가 결정됐다고 언급하며 로던이 캐스팅되기를 바란다고 밝히기도 했다. 이후 칼럼 터너가 유력 후보로 부상했지만, 패틴슨과 니콜라스 홀트의 오디션 소식이 알려지면서 경쟁 구도는 다시 달라졌다. 이 밖에도 조시 오코너, 톰 프랜시스, 에런 테일러존슨, 해리스 디킨슨, 가수 해리 스타일스 등이 후보로 거론됐다. 버라이어티는 패틴슨이 올해 할리우드에서 가장 주목받는 배우 중 한 명이라는 점이 캐스팅에 영향을 미쳤을 것으로 분석했다. 패틴슨은 올해 젠데이아와 함께 출연한 영화 '더 드라마(The Drama)'로 제작비 2800만달러 대비 약 1억3400만달러의 전 세계 흥행 수익을 올렸다. 또 범죄 실화 프로그램 진행자 크리스 핸슨을 연기한 '프라임타임(Primetime)'은 제작비 1800만달러로 약 6100만달러의 흥행 수익을 기록했다. 크리스토퍼 놀런 감독의 '오디세이'에서도 주요 배역인 안티노오스를 맡았으며, 해당 작품은 전 세계에서 18억달러의 흥행 수익을 거뒀다. 패틴슨은 대형 프랜차이즈를 이끈 경험도 갖추고 있다. 2022년 개봉한 '더 배트맨'에서 브루스 웨인 역을 맡았으며, 2028년 개봉 예정인 후속작에도 items.t: California state AG sues OpenAI over rogue agent incidents
items.d: The California lawsuit represents one of the first attempts to hold an AI lab legally accountable for a rogue agent incident.
items.fullText: OpenAI is facing a new lawsuit from the California Attorney General’s office , alleging that the company’s training practices and lax security pose an ongoing danger to the public. At the center of the case is the July 2026 Hugging Face compromise , in which a pre-release model within OpenAI compromised both companies’ security systems to complete a training benchmark. In its official report on the incident , OpenAI called it “an outlier scenario involving a rare and unexpected confluence of events.” The California lawsuit represents one of the first attempts by a government regulator to hold an AI lab legally accountable for a rogue agent incident, with significant implications for both OpenAI’s competitors and its clients. The complaint centers on the Hugging Face incident, but also cites similar incidents involving RubyGems , DseWiki , the Wikimedia Foundation , and Australian government websites as evidence that the underlying behavior is ongoing. The complaint also alleges that dozens of similar incidents have occurred without public disclosure. “OpenAI has recently sent notices to dozens of additional third parties whose websites or internal systems have been infiltrated by OpenAI agents,” the complaint reads. “In some cases, OpenAI agents were able to access sensitive personally identifiable information, such as employee records containing names, birth dates, addresses, and more. The vast majority of these incidents have not been disclosed or discussed publicly by either OpenAI or by the affected third parties.” The central allegation is that OpenAI’s ongoing testing practices constitute a public nuisance because the lack of safety controls present an ongoing risk to the public. A secondary claim alleges unfair competition stemming from the marketing of an unsafe product. items.t: Uber says hackers stole information on close to 150,000 driver’s licenses during data breach
items.d: The ride-sharing giant said driver's license information stored by AI cloud company Fireworks AI was stolen during a security incident.
items.fullText: Uber is notifying close to 150,000 drivers that their personal and driver’s license information was stolen during an October data breach at one of the company’s tech providers. In notices filed this week with several U.S. attorneys general, including California and Iowa , the ride-hailing giant said it was notified on October 9 by the provider that hackers broke in and stole internal credentials, which were used to access Uber’s data. The company said it subsequently began notifying affected drivers that their personal information was stored with the provider. The stolen data includes affected drivers’ names, addresses, dates of birth, and driver’s license numbers. TechCrunch has learned that the provider is Fireworks AI, which lets developers access and use open-weight AI models. Fireworks reported a data breach last month in which hackers stole its customers’ information, including billing data and some private AI datasets. Online productivity startup Notion and AI coding startup Cursor have both confirmed that they had data stolen during the Fireworks hack. In Uber’s case, the company said it had alerts enabled to detect unauthorized access to its Fireworks environment, but because the hackers used Fireworks’ own internal credentials, “no alerts were triggered.” When reached for comment, an Uber spokesperson told TechCrunch: “The notices to drivers are in relation to a security incident impacting one of our third-party vendors, Fireworks.ai, which had access to some Uber data,” and deferred our questions to Fireworks. A spokesperson for Fireworks confirmed that the company identified a security issue involving unauthorized access to some of its systems, which affected customer data, but the spokesperson did not address our questions about the incident. items.t: California sues ChatGPT maker OpenAI over rogue hacking incidents
items.d: California Attorney General Rob Bonta filed a sweeping lawsuit against OpenAI on Monday, alleging the technology giant jeopardized public safety by creating AI models “without the safeguards and monitoring necessary to adequately protect” people.
items.fullText: Artificial intelligence California sues ChatGPT maker OpenAI over rogue hacking incidents California Attorney General Rob Bonta’s lawsuit alleges OpenAI has created AI models without proper safeguards. Listen to this article with a free profile 00:00 00:00 OpenAI logo. Samuel Boivin / NurPhoto via Getty Share Add NBC News to Google Nov. 16, 2026, 1:52 PM EST / Updated Nov. 16, 2026, 2:34 PM EST By Daniel Arkin California Attorney General Rob Bonta filed a sweeping lawsuit against OpenAI on Monday, alleging the technology giant jeopardized public safety by creating AI models “without the safeguards and monitoring necessary to adequately protect” people. The suit centers on a July incident involving hundreds of autonomous AI agents created by OpenAI that attacked computer systems at Hugging Face , a separate AI company. Bonta’s office alleges the attack was “entirely foreseeable in light of OpenAI’s choice to test models it knew to be dangerous in a flawed and exploitable testing environment without proper oversight.” Bonta’s office further alleges the ChatGPT developer’s failure to secure the testing of its models created a “public nuisance” and violated California’s Unfair Competition Law, a broad consumer protection statute. In response to a request for comment, OpenAI spokesperson Drew Pusateri said the company has “undertaken an extensive and transparent effort to understand and address misaligned model activity” since the Hugging Face incident. items.fullText: Lambda Boosts AI Factory Resiliency and Efficiency With NVIDIA Photonics November 16, 2026 by Brian Sparks 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! To train an AI model, thousands of GPUs have to work together, requiring a network that’s fast, efficient and resilient. Lambda is tackling the network piece of the puzzle with NVIDIA Photonics co-packaged optics (CPO) switches. The cloud provider is using the switches to connect NVIDIA GB300 NVL72 racks with more than 10,000 GPUs, delivering lower power, higher resiliency and longer mean time between interruptions (MTBI) to an AI factory at scale. “Networking has to keep pace with the demands of increasingly large AI clusters,” said Dave Ward, president of cloud services at Lambda. “Bringing co-packaged optics into a deployment of this scale is an important step toward building the infrastructure needed to support the next generation of AI.” Read All NVIDIA Announcements From SC26 In the company’s tests using the switches, network latency — the time needed for moving data — dropped by about 4% at rack scale and by up to about 10% at pod scale. Across rack, scalable unit and pod configurations, the network maintains the same throughput as conventional pluggable optics. Delivering Power Efficiency and Resiliency at Scale Improving power efficiency and resiliency matters because the network sits at the center of AI factory productivity. In a large training job, one interrupted link can stall thousands of GPUs. With agentic inference, one network disruption can introduce cascading latency effects on many agents. Every interruption costs time, and every watt spent on networking is a watt not available for compute. NVIDIA Photonics addresses both power efficiency and resiliency. By replacing pluggable transceivers with co-packaged optical engines on the switch package, it delivers up to 5x better power efficiency and up to 15x higher reliability than conventional pluggable optics. items.fullText: NVIDIA Expands Open Source Commitment With OpenShell Contribution and New AI Infrastructure At KubeCon, NVIDIA is putting tools to secure agents and run AI on Kubernetes in the hands of the cloud-native community. November 10, 2026 by Warren Barkley 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! Kubernetes, the open source system that manages how applications run across thousands of AI factories, has become the foundation for AI, and the demands on it are only growing. To help meet them, NVIDIA is deepening its commitment to open source at KubeCon + CloudNativeCon , the flagship conference for the Kubernetes and cloud-native communities. NVIDIA is contributing NVIDIA OpenShell , an open source runtime for securing and governing autonomous agents, to the Cloud Native Computing Foundation (CNCF), a nonprofit that is part of the Linux Foundation and the host of KubeCon. As a CNCF Sandbox project, OpenShell will be governed by the organizations building it into their products and strengthened by the expertise of security professionals worldwide. NVIDIA is also contributing to Agent Substrate , an open source Google-led framework for operating long-running agent workloads at scale on Kubernetes that has been accepted into the CNCF Sandbox. Additionally, NVIDIA announced new components of the NVIDIA DSX AI Factory Platform : NVIDIA Kubernetes Engine , NVIDIA Kubernetes Recipes and NVIDIA Snapshot . These tools help teams deploy, manage and scale GPU infrastructure on Kubernetes for AI factories. Together, these advancements mark a step forward in making Kubernetes the leading foundation for AI workloads at scale — empowering developers to build safer, more efficient AI infrastructure for the future.
